content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Jacob Santos (E050) requests write access to Source Code.

Notes:
- Notes 1-5 say he's a full-time Engineer, recommend write.
- Note 6 (Security) says Security DB shows he's a contractor with basic security training, recommends read.

The access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns the system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

The conflict: Most agents say full-time. Security agent looked up in their own database and found contractor with basic security training, and they noted the others didn't look up employment type in their own databases (they used team records).

Note 6 says "Security DB shows E050 (Jacob Santos) is a contractor with BASIC security training, not full-time." Note 6 also says "not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1..." for role, but employment type and security training were looked up.

So the security agent is the only one who actually looked up employment type in their own database. Notes 2-5 explicitly say employment type was NOT looked up in own database; they used team records.

So the most reliable info: Security DB says contractor, basic training. As a contractor with basic training, max access is read. Requested write is above max, so grant read.

The policy for contractors: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. Basic training → read only.

So the decision should be read.

Let me submit the decision: read.
